segments.text: American Fork City Council — Work Session — June 7, 2022:

Finance Director Anna Montoya presented a budget adding three full-time police officers and two part-time records specialists, equivalent to one full-time position. She said the proposed property-tax increase would fund increased public-safety costs and road improvements.

entities.label: Three police officers, records staffing, and tax funding

segments.text: The proposed budget tied additional police and records staffing to increased public-safety costs and a proposed property-tax increase.
Relevant passages from the official meeting minutes:

Ms. Montoya gave an overview of the personnel changes by function. The proposal included reorganizing in Administration and Community services and adding a full-time Community Service Director which is currently vacant. They were proposing a full-time Arborist (split 75% from the General Fund and 25% in Irrigation). Also, additional staff for Library, Parks, and Senior Center. Some of that is offset by additional revenue. In Public Safety, they were proposing 4.5 additional FTE - 3 full-time police officers, 2 part-time records specialists in Police department, and move a part-time Deputy Fire Marshall to full-time. The 2 part-time records will equal one full-time FTE. Public Works is proposing 1.25 for a full-time Public Works technician in the Streets department and moving a part-time administrative assistant to full-time. In Development Services, they were adding one full-time planner and moving a part-time to full-time for administrative assistant due to the workload and development. In Utilities 1.25 was mostly in storm drain. It has one full-time coordinator and one full-time inspector. They were also proposing a full-time Public Works technician in Water that will be split between Culinary and Irrigation. The total is 14.8 of FTE which is a 5% increase overall.

Ms. Montoya discussed property tax, per previous work session, looking at a $10 per month per household which equates to $120 a year. She showed the proposed public notice. She mentioned the certified tax rate should be received next week. She guessed the proposed rate will be less than pegging the rate due to inflation and the rise of evaluations but won’t now know for certain until we receive the certified tax rate. The increase from property tax will go to fund the increased public safety costs and road improvements.
